public_rationale: Marcus said withdrawing Galactica could not contain the technology because the model had been open-sourced and the method published, and because ChatGPT was out. On 17 November 2022 Meta said it had paused only the demo and that its models stayed available so researchers could reproduce the paper's results. In early December ChatGPT was publicly available and widely used. During the period he described, taking down the demo did not remove access to the technology.
limitations: Shows availability during the period, not long-term containment.
Weight availability rests on Meta's statement as reported, not a dated repository record.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Misinformation-capable LLM technology can no longer be contained or withdrawn.

statement.excerpt: Alas, the genie can no longer be stuffed back in the bottle.

from_speaker: the genie can no longer be stuffed back in the bottle
MetaAI initially open-sourced the model, and published a paper
anyone skilled in the art can now replicate their recipe
our_interpretation: I read this as a claim about the situation when he wrote it (mid-November to 10 December 2022). Taking down Galactica's demo did not take the technology out of circulation: the model and paper stayed available, and ChatGPT was publicly accessible.
Target period runs from Galactica's release (2022-11-15) to the post date (2022-12-10).
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that after the demo came down, Galactica's model or paper stayed available for others to use or replicate, and/or that similar systems stayed publicly accessible.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that Meta withdrew the Galactica weights and paper completely and that no comparable model was publicly available in that period.
